feature: blind bid rounds on chain: `open_round`, `commit_bid` (sealed hash, approved merchants only, before the commit deadline), `reveal_bid` (must open the commitment, before the reveal deadline), `round_best_quote` (only after the reveal deadline); 30 merchant agents bid through it

feature: NEAR AI Cloud inference for every merchant pitch and the buyer's cited "why", response signatures verified
detail: plain TLS, 33/33 response signatures verified in a recorded live run

feature: NEAR AI issues the verdict under E2EE v2: the facts go sealed to the attested model key, the model derives the predicates and echoes a binding of the envelope, and `make verify` checks the TDX quote (dcap-qvl, Intel root, committed PCS collateral), report_data (signing key and our nonce), the TEE signature over the exact wire bytes, the sealed answer (opened with a disclosed one-time key), predicates equal to the code's, and the binding
detail: one live capture on synthetic facts (chat `08af1d014f2d4f379dba94094562d9ba`, TCB UpToDate). On chain, `submit_near_ai_verdict` accepts it only with a registered model attestation (same nonce), the TEE signature over the exact response bytes, and a sealed answer that opens with the disclosed key and echoes this envelope's binding; `make verify` runs the contract on it and on 4 refusals. The quote check itself happens before `register_model_attestation`, not in the contract; NVIDIA GPU evidence is not checked

feature: OutLayer worker as referee: signed result (<= 900 bytes) checked by the contract with `ed25519_verify`; `settle` requires the receipt
detail: in `make verify`; not deployed to OutLayer yet (the register step waits on a founder OK). Live `estimate_execution_cost` = 0.0070001 NEAR

feature: dispute arbiter: re-checks citations and every signature, signs upheld or overturned; an overturned receipt is cleared and settle is blocked
detail: `make verify` check 22; a threshold of distinct arbiter signatures (`set_arbiter_threshold`, `submit_dispute_decisions`, 4 contract tests) is built; the live bazaar runs at threshold 1 with one arbiter key, held by REP

feature: World ID "one person, one agent": the contract checks a verifier's ed25519 attestation and binds one agent per World nullifier; `world_id_human` needs it
detail: on testnet with a placeholder action and our verifier key; the live World ID service (rep-world-verify) is not wired

feature: sealed reviews (Semaphore v4): a settled purchase joins the merchant's group (LeanIMT, Poseidon on chain); during a round a member posts a sealed rating with a Groth16 proof checked on `alt_bn128` host functions, one per member per round (nullifier scoped to merchant and round); after the round members reveal, only if the group has k >= 5; release is batched and sorted by hash; `best_quote` breaks price ties by the score and takes a `min_score` floor
detail: 2 rounds of 6 sealed ratings released on testnet; 13 contract tests on real Semaphore proofs

feature: conserved delegation: standing flows from a merchant's released ratings along hire edges to the sub-agents it hires (w = 1/2), following a design rule in REP's draft "(an unpublished REP draft)": the whole chain gets at most w/(1-w) of the seed
detail: standing flowed from m01's released ratings to m02 and m03 on testnet; property test over random graphs with rings

feature: verifiable compute (Jolt zkVM), four guests: standing graph, price stack, referee, cohort k >= 5. The contract keeps the graph root and per-cohort roots; for the graph, the contract keeps a hash-chained root of the standing graph and accepts score updates only from the registered Jolt program, for the current root, signed by a worker that verified the proof off chain
detail: all four guests proved and verified (prove 1.3 to 9 s, verify about 60 ms, proofs 80 to 93 KB); standing proved twice over the live graph and posted on testnet

feature: NEP-366 meta-tx relayer for `submit_review` and `reveal_review`: the rater signs with a one-time key, the relayer pays gas (gasless rating)
detail: the relayer pays every demo purchase and every rating (demo and review policies), delegate actions on testnet

feature: FUNCTION CALL KEYS: agent key limited to `settle` (a function-call key cannot attach a deposit, so `submit_verdict` and `withdraw` stay with the full-access key)

detail: (a model, assumptions stated)

feature: sealed verdicts (hashes only on chain): the issuer signs an envelope with no predicates, tier or cap in the clear and a `disclosure` commitment to them; the opening goes to the referee, which prices from it and refuses a price over the hidden cap; the contract accepts only a receipt price its own schedule code can produce for some predicate subset (the World discount only for a World-bound agent)

Authenticated `api.github.com/user` notarized with MPC-TLS through the REP notary (pinned key, not attested), 3 fields revealed, the facts sealed to NEAR AI (E2EE v2), a sealed verdict, a `github_builder` line that wins a blind round, one dUSDC settle, `make leak` before and after

feature: trust anchors under a DAO and a timelock: a Sputnik DAO owns a test bazaar (one council vote is refused, two apply); every anchor change (issuers, model keys, referee, arbiters, World verifier, arbiter threshold, fee, Jolt program, a lower TCB floor) is queued for a public delay, executable by anyone after it and cancellable inside it

feature: a buying group's own treasury: a Sputnik DAO created per group, its council the members; each member pledges the tier price, which stays in the bazaar under the group; only a passed DAO proposal refunds a member or pays the merchant, never below the tier's member count

feature: market fee into a DAO treasury: at most 2%, taken from the price (merchant + fee = price), in the liability record, given back on a failed payout, swept by anyone to the treasury; a raise waits out the anchor timelock
detail: 1% on testnet, swept to the Sputnik DAO `bookerbob-gov.sputnikv2.testnet`; 5 contract tests

feature: certified private eval (the envelope's second use): a model answers a sealed 20-item set on NEAR AI Cloud, each answer's TEE signature is checked, code grades, a registered issuer signs the certificate; the bazaar stores the floored score and answers `eval_passes(subject, set, threshold)`
detail: glm-5.3-flash scored 20/20 (bucket 100) on testnet; the items stay private; 5 contract tests

feature: REP Eval, calibrated: 120 sealed items at 4 levels, 3 NEAR AI models in a 400-token budget, every answer TEE-signed, grading and a bootstrap 95% CI in the worker's code, one certificate per model from a separate eval issuer key; a leaderboard page reads the scores from chain
detail: headline on a held-out set made after the protocol was frozen: glm-5.3-flash 58/120 (CI 39.2 to 56.7), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 112/120, Qwen3.6-35B 0/120 (budget-bound, out of tokens on every item); all 360 TEE signatures valid; the tuned calibration set's run is on chain too and within 3 items; `make eval-verify` in about a second. Only one model lands in the 40 to 80% band. v2 (protocol frozen first): 60 referee-claim items, truth from the referee's code, set committed by its own owner account with `commit_eval_set`: glm 44/60, DeepSeek 35/60, Qwen a budget probe at 0; every answer given was right, every miss a reply cut at 600 tokens; v3, the same items at 2,000 tokens (frozen first): DeepSeek 58/60, glm 55/60, again right on every answer given, so the set is too easy to separate them by accuracy
